item.title: The Fed is poised to raise rates, a vital oil pipeline shuts down and Sen. Susan Collins has some strong words for Trump. Read more in today’s What’s News newsletter:
item.content:encoded: Plus, a vital oil pipeline shuts down and Sen. Susan Collins has some strong words for Trump.

item.title: Treasury Yields, Fed Rate-Hike Bets Rise After Strong U.S. Jobs Data
item.content:encoded: U.S. Treasury yields jump after significantly stronger-than-expected employment data for August lifted expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the Sept. 16 meeting.

item.title: BOE Survey Points to Cooling Price Pressures
item.content:encoded: Businesses expect the prices they charge to rise by 3.8% over the coming 12 months, a decrease from the 3.9% expected in July.

item.title: Swiss Inflation Jumps on Higher Energy Prices
item.content:encoded: Swiss inflation jumped in August, reversing several months of cooling price growth as renewed tensions in the Middle East pushed global energy costs higher.

item.title: U.S. Home Price Growth Rose in June
item.content:encoded: The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller National Home Price Index rose 1.5% in the 12 months through June, compared with a 1.2% increase in May.

item.title: U.S. Housing Starts Dropped in July
item.content:encoded: Housing starts fell sharply below expectations in July as home-builder sentiment remained muted.

item.title: The ECB raised interest rates for the second time this year, as resurgent energy prices reignited concerns over inflation
item.content:encoded: Resurgent oil and gas prices have reignited concerns over price pressures.

item.title: Turkish Central Bank Keeps Rates Unchanged Amid Continued Inflation Risks
item.content:encoded: The bank held its benchmark one-week repo rate at 37.0%, it said Thursday. The bank last cut its key rate in January.

item.title: Eurozone Retail Sales Retreat as Consumers Still Fret Over War
item.content:encoded: Retail sales in the eurozone fell in June and was the second decline in the four full months since the start of the war against Iran.

item.title: The latest Canadian tariffs on $20 billion of U.S. exports went into effect Tuesday. A handful of U.S. states are likely to feel a big effect.
item.content:encoded: The latest Canadian tariffs on $20 billion of U.S. exports went into effect Tuesday. A handful of U.S. states are likely to feel a big effect.

item.title: Investors have all but concluded the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week for the first time in three years. The harder question is what comes after that.
item.content:encoded: Investors have started pricing in a series of increases. Chairman Kevin Warsh’s aversion to signaling the path leaves him few tools to talk them out of it

item.title: U.S. Stocks Gain as Inflation Figure Boosts Odds of Rate Hike
item.content:encoded: U.S. stocks climbed, a signal that investors like the idea of a Federal Reserve rate hike tamping down inflation.

item.title: U.S. Mortgage Rates Top 7% For First Time in 15 Months
item.content:encoded: Rates had steadily tumbled to about 6% in late February, but reversed when the U.S. and Israel started the war in Iran, disrupting oil shipments and driving up inflation.

item.title: Last month, the U.S. added an impressive 162,000 jobs and unemployment is low, but broad economic measures might be missing how much Americans’ costs have risen—and how many of them haven’t kept up
item.content:encoded: Official data shows steady growth and low unemployment but misses how rising costs have left many Americans behind.

item.title: A jittery Treasury market and the prospect of Fed rate increases risk making life more expensive for already cost-pressured Americans
item.content:encoded: A jittery Treasury market and the prospect of Fed rate increases risk making life more expensive for already cost-pressured Americans.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Has Dropped in August, per Michigan Survey
item.content:encoded: Consumers’ economic mood is weaker this month versus July, according to preliminary results from the University of Michigan’s monthly survey.

item.title: Retail Sales Fell Last Month
item.content:encoded: Retailers’ sales fell by 0.6% last month to $763.6 billion, versus the 0.2% growth recorded in June.

item.title: Canada Tribunal Rules U.S. Canned Vegetable Imports Hurt Domestic Food Sector
item.content:encoded: The tribunal recommended a three-year tariff-rate quota on imported canned vegetables from certain countries, led by the U.S.

item.title: President Trump signed orders to ban the importation of many dairy products, alcoholic beverages and motorcycles from Canada in three weeks
item.content:encoded: The ban will affect a small subset of industries but could be ruinous for those companies if the trade prohibitions go into effect in three weeks.

item.title: Three numbers show how China’s extraordinary export surge is on track to at least match last year’s record $1.2 trillion surplus
item.content:encoded: The country’s extraordinary export surge puts it on track to at least match last year’s record $1.2 trillion surplus.
